A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain complete main text and Appendices A–L. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original causal-extraction, clustering, frame-prediction, human-evaluation, and SHAP analysis results in Sections 4–5 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical outcomes, including clustering comparisons in Table 3, classifier results in Table 12, and appendix human evaluations.

M1.justification: The extraction, verbalization, character-role annotation, constrained clustering, and schema-attribution procedures remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1 and the appendix prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Media Frames Corpus immigration and gun-control coverage, plus ESC and MavenERE causality evaluations in Appendix E.1. No datasets, domains, or tasks are added or removed.

E2.justification: The same k-means comparisons appear in the clustering and intrusion evaluations. The teacher–DAPrompt evaluation and RoBERTa versus narrative-feature classifier comparison are also retained.

E3.justification: Reported sampling, preprocessing, frame-label selection, cluster counts, constraint weights, splits, metrics, training settings, and human-evaluation procedures match across Sections 4–5 and Appendices D–F.

E4.justification: The cluster-size analysis, intrusion tests, schema-quality assessment, five-category error analysis, and instance-, frame-, and domain-level SHAP analyses are retained. Redrawing their figures adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five DAPrompt seeds and mean/standard-deviation summaries in Table 8, together with unchanged annotation-agreement statistics, confidence intervals, and significance reporting.

E6.justification: Numerical tables and the redrawn SHAP plots retain their values, rankings, and findings. For example, structured clustering's all-chain frame F1 remains 42.32 for immigration and 41.68 for gun control in Table 3.

T1.justification: The clustering objective, initialization criterion, purity and feature definitions, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Parenthesis corrections in example causal triplets are typographic, without changing mathematical meaning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint event–character modeling, scalable and interpretable schema induction, improved clustering, and alignment with framing theory.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the intrusion results, pipeline errors, and SHAP patterns are unchanged. The limitations concerning English-language U.S. news, simplified character roles, static narratives, and classifier performance are also retained.

D1.justification: The code link, model specifications, implementation and training details, appendix prompts, hardware disclosures, and approximately ten-day pipeline runtime remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and novelty positioning remain unchanged, including the claimed contribution of combining detailed character-level and event-level information.

P1.justification: v2 corrects causal-triplet parentheses in Tables 1 and 11 and changes figure wording from 'narrative themes' to 'narrative schemas.' The version stamp changes, while the main prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 2, and 4–9 use higher-resolution graphics. SHAP plots adjust typography, spacing, and some axis ticks, causing local text reflow in Appendix F. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Sharper diagrams, particularly Figure 2, and clearer SHAP plot typography make the existing content easier to inspect. Corrected triplet parentheses also improve notation consistency. These are limited presentation gains; the methods, empirical evidence, claims, and limitations remain unchanged.
